title: Teams and Microsoft 365 admin centres: unified agent and app availability across Teams, Outlook and Microsoft 365 Copilot
summary: The briefing passes: the rollout phases, administrator roles, navigation paths and PowerShell calls are supported by the supplied notice and Microsoft documentation. Two minor corrections remain: cite the custom-app upload cmdlet reference, and remove the catalogue-export checklist instruction because it has no controls-table row.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Scope: Surfaces
claims.claim: The change unifies agent and app availability across Teams, Outlook and Microsoft 365 Copilot.
claims.quote: With this change, app and agent availability  will be unified across Teams, Outlook and Microsoft 365 copilot.

claims.claim: Before this update, Integrated Apps changes in the Microsoft 365 admin center affected these apps only in Outlook and Microsoft 365 Copilot.
claims.quote: Before this update, changes made through the Integrated Apps section in the Microsoft 365 admin center would only affect these apps on Outlook and the Microsoft 365 copilot

claims.where: What's changing: first paragraph; Why it matters
claims.claim: Before this update, changes in the Teams admin center affected only Teams.
claims.quote: similarly, changes made in the Teams admin center would exclusively affect Teams.

claims.where: What's changing: first paragraph; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Once a tenant is unified, org-wide settings changes synchronise between both admin centres.
claims.quote: After your tenant is unified, all changes to org-wide settings, agent app, status, or availability in TAC are automatically synchronized in MAC and vice versa.

claims.where: What's changing: first paragraph; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Once a tenant is unified, agent and app status changes synchronise between both admin centres.

claims.quote: Ensures consistent and synchronized agent and app behavior across platforms, as changes to app availability settings in one admin center are automatically synced with the other

claims.claim: The notice places the beginning of Phase 1 rollout at the end of September 2025.
claims.quote: We will begin rolling out this feature at the end of September 2025.

claims.where: What's changing: second paragraph; Scope: Who gets it
claims.claim: Tenants that never modified org-wide defaults, app availability or app block/unblock settings in either admin centre are unified automatically.
claims.quote: If your tenant never modified its org-wide defaults, app availability, or app block or unblock settings in either TAC or MAC, then your tenant's app availability policies are automatically unified.

claims.where: What's changing: second paragraph; Scope: Who gets it
claims.claim: Phase 2 targets tenants that previously modified org-wide defaults, app availability or block/unblock settings in either admin centre.
claims.quote: This phase targets tenants that have previously modified their organization-wide defaults, app availability, or block/unblock settings in either admin center.

claims.where: What's changing: second paragraph; Scope: Who gets it
claims.claim: The notice says Phase 2 has fully rolled out.
claims.quote: This phase has been fully rolled out to all tenants. Tenants can choose to align through the wizard experience available in Teams admin center.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: The current Phase 2 move for modified tenants is admin-opt-in and changes no org-wide or app-level setting without administrator action.
claims.quote: Tenants can choose to align through the wizard experience available in Teams admin center. Note: In this phase, no changes will be applied to org-wide settings or app-level settings without administrator action.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Scope; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Phase 3 will automatically unify availability for tenants that have not taken action.
claims.quote: Tenants that have not taken action to unify availability through the wizard experience released in Phase 1 and Phase 2 will have their availability automatically unified across MAC and TAC as part of this phase.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Scope; Open questions
claims.claim: The supplied notice gives no date for Phase 3.
claims.quote: The Phase 3 timeline will be announced separately, at least 60 days before that phase begins.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft promises Phase 3 timeline information at least 60 days before it begins.
claims.quote: We will inform customers of the timeline and additional details at least 60 days in advance before this phase begins.

claims.claim: The notice text includes an update dated 18 November 2026.
claims.quote: Updated November 18, 2026: Unified app and agent installation management is now generally available.

claims.claim: Installation management is unified within 24 to 48 hours after a tenant completes availability unification.
claims.quote: For any tenant that unifies app/agent availability through Phase 1, Phase 2, or Phase 3, app and agent installations are also unified across the Microsoft 365 admin center (MAC) and Teams admin center (TAC) within 24–48 hours of completing availability unification.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Installations previously made through Teams app setup policies are not unified by this change.
claims.quote: Important: App installation is no longer managed through Teams app setup policies. Installations previously made through those policies are not unified as part of this change.

claims.claim: Learn's unified management page points to roadmap ID 485712 for timelines.
claims.quote: For timelines, see Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 485712.

claims.claim: A modified tenant without availability differences is asked to consent to unified app management.
claims.quote: Select Move to unified app management. A dialog box appears to ask for your consent to move to the unified agent and app management experience.

claims.where: What's changing: wizard paragraph; Risk assessment; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: A tenant with differences first chooses the org-wide settings to apply on the Align org-wide app settings page.
claims.quote: The Align org-wide app settings page appears. Here you can select the org-wide default settings that you want to apply across TAC and MAC.

claims.where: What's changing: wizard paragraph; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The wizard allows individual resolution of app status and availability differences.
claims.quote: Individual app-alignment: Select any individual app and review the App status and Availability. Go to Review settings for the selected app to check the App status and Availability.

claims.where: What's changing: wizard paragraph; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The wizard allows bulk resolution using settings from either admin centre.
claims.quote: Bulk app resolution: Select multiple apps at a time and select either Teams admin center or Microsoft 365 admin center from the Apply settings from drop-down list.

claims.claim: The wizard can download app status and availability comparisons as CSV.
claims.quote: Download the CSV file: Select the Excel icon in the top-right corner to download the App status and Availability settings as a CSV file.

claims.where: controls[0].note; What's changing; Risk assessment; Scope; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Any Teams or Global admin can prepare changes up to the Review summary page.
claims.quote: Any Teams or Global admin can make updates upto the Review summary page.

claims.where: controls[0].note; What's changing; Risk assessment; Scope; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Only a Global admin can give consent and apply the final unification changes.
claims.quote: Only a Global admin can give consent and apply the final changes.

claims.claim: Learn lists avoiding mismatched configurations as a purpose of unification.
claims.quote: Avoids mismatched configurations

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Choosing one admin centre's differing per-app status and availability applies that choice across the unified admin centres.
claims.quote: Select the admin center’s settings that you want to apply from the Apply settings from drop-down list and select Apply settings.

claims.claim: The roadmap description concerns availability management rather than specifying which data agents and apps read.
claims.quote: Administrators using the Microsoft 365 admin center and Teams admin center who manage agents and apps that work across Teams, Outlook and the Microsoft 365 copilot will be able to apply their changes consistently across all these surfaces.

claims.claim: A single third-party org-wide control manages bulk availability of both new and existing third-party agents and apps.
claims.quote: Under Third-party apps, a single control manages the bulk availability of both the new and existing third-party agents and apps.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Availability changes take up to 24 hours to take effect.
claims.quote: It takes up to 24 hours for the availability changes to take effect.

claims.claim: In rare cases availability changes take up to six days to appear in the client.
claims.quote: In rare cases, it might take up to six days for the changes to reflect in the client.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Each organisational user needs a Teams licence before using Teams.
claims.quote: Except for joining Teams meetings anonymously, each user in your organization must have a Teams license before they can use Teams.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Joining Teams meetings anonymously is an exception to the Teams licence requirement.
claims.quote: Except for joining Teams meetings anonymously, each user in your organization must have a Teams license before they can use Teams.

claims.claim: The licensing model is included, with the existing Teams licence requirement named in the notes.
claims.quote: You manage access to Teams at the user level by assigning or removing a Microsoft Teams product license.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No licence specific to availability unification is published as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: unified agent app availability management licensing price meter charge. Opened learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/uam-tac-mac, user-access and manage-apps; these give no unification-specific licence.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Scope: Roles; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Learn names the Teams Administrator role as the requirement for using Teams admin center.
claims.quote: To use Teams admin center, you must have a Teams Administrator role. Some admins with a higher privilege role can accomplish agent and app governance tasks

claims.claim: The cited pages document no meter or charge for unification itself.
claims.quote: Searched: unified agent app availability management licensing price meter charge. Opened learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/uam-tac-mac, manage-apps and user-access; none names a unification meter or charge.

claims.claim: Paid app publisher charges are service subscriptions for app functionality, separate from the unification operation.
claims.quote: Some Teams apps require purchasing a service subscription to use app functionality. These service subscriptions are called Software as a Service (SaaS) offers.

claims.claim: Administrators can view and manage only agents and apps deployed in their tenant's release channel.
claims.quote: You can only view and manage agents and apps that are deployed in the same release channel as your tenant is.

claims.claim: The unification entry point is Teams admin center > Teams apps > Manage apps > Move to unified app management.
claims.quote: Go to Teams apps > Manage apps. Select Move to unified app management.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents no cmdlet or API that runs the move to unified app management.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams unified app management move unification wizard PowerShell Microsoft Graph API automation; "unified app management" "PowerShell" "migration"; "unified app management" "Graph". Opened learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/uam-tac-mac and the Update-M365TeamsApp reference.

claims.claim: Per-app availability is at Teams apps > Manage apps > app > Users and groups > Select to manage who this app is installed for or available to in your organization > Availability > Edit availability > Available to.
claims.quote: Select the Users and groups tab. Under Select to manage who this app is installed for or available to in your organization, select Availability. Select Edit availability. Select the required option from Available to menu.

claims.claim: Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <app id> -AppAssignmentType Everyone sets the app's availability to Everyone.
claims.quote:
Update-M365TeamsApp -Id 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b -AppAssignmentType Everyone
Updates the availability value for Bookings app (App ID 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b) to Everyone.

claims.claim: AppAssignmentType supports Everyone, UsersAndGroups and Noone.
claims.quote:
-AppAssignmentType
App availability type.
Parameter sets
(Everyone
UsersandGroups
Noone)

claims.claim: An app can be allowed or blocked at Teams admin center > Teams apps > Manage apps > app > Allow or Block.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Teams admin center and access Teams apps > Manage apps. Select the app on the Manage apps page and select Allow or Block option.

claims.claim: Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <app id> -IsBlocked $true changes the app's tenant state.
claims.quote:
Update-M365TeamsApp -Id 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b -IsBlocked $true
Unblocks Bookings app (App ID 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b).

claims.claim: The reference describes IsBlocked as the state of the app in the tenant.
claims.quote:
-IsBlocked
The state of the app in the tenant.
Type: Boolean

claims.claim: The reference labels its example using -IsBlocked $true as unblocking.
claims.quote:
Update-M365TeamsApp -Id 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b -IsBlocked $true
Unblocks Bookings app (App ID 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b).

claims.claim: Org-wide availability defaults are at Teams apps > Manage apps > Actions > Org-wide app settings > app type > Let users install and use available apps by default.
claims.quote: On Manage apps page, under the Actions menu, select Org-wide app settings. ... Under Custom apps, turn off or turn on Let users install and use available apps by default option.

claims.claim: No automation for these org-wide availability defaults is documented as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: MicrosoftTeams PowerShell org-wide default app availability Microsoft third-party custom apps Set Teams settings; Microsoft Graph beta Teams org-wide app default availability settings API. Read manage-apps, app-centric-management, Set-CsTeamsSettingsCustomApp and Graph settings excerpts.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsSettingsCustomApp controls custom-app uploading rather than the availability-default switch.
claims.quote: If the isSideloadedAppsInteractionEnabled is set to true, the switch is enabled. So that the custom apps can be uploaded as app packages and available in the organization's app store, vice versa.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoftteams/set-csteamssettingscustomapp?view=teams-ps to sources with title 'Set-CsTeamsSettingsCustomApp'; it supports the distinction in controls[3].note.

claims.claim: Org-wide app setting changes take effect after a few hours.
claims.quote: Select Save. The settings take effect after a few hours.

claims.where: Governance controls; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: An org-wide availability-default change does not override individually saved per-app availability assignments.
claims.quote: Your change to the org-wide app setting applies only to those apps for which you didn't change the availability.

claims.claim: Update-M365TeamsApp belongs to the MicrosoftTeams PowerShell module.
claims.quote: Module: MicrosoftTeams PowerShell module

claims.claim: The Update-M365TeamsApp reference also documents modifying installation status.
claims.quote: This cmdlet allows administrators to modify app state, availability and installation status by adding or removing users and groups or changing assignment type or installation status.

claims.where: Governance controls: final paragraph; Open questions
claims.claim: The Update-M365TeamsApp reference does not mention unified management or explicitly say that its changes synchronise to the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: Searched: "unified app management" "PowerShell" "migration"; "unified app management" "Graph". Read the complete learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoftteams/update-m365teamsapp reference; it contains neither unified-management wording nor a cross-admin-centre synchronisation statement.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout, catalogue-export bullet
claims.claim: The Teams admin center can export the agent and app catalogue as CSV, including status and availability.
claims.quote:
Export agent and app catalog as CSV
As an admin, you can export the entire agent and app catalog for your org from the Teams admin center. It can help you to coordinate with admin and security teams to evaluate agents and apps, verify availability, verify status, and more.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout, catalogue-export bullet
claims.claim: The checklist instructs administrators to export the catalogue, but the controls table contains no catalogue-export row.
claims.quote: Export the agent and app catalogue from the Teams admin center as CSV. The four controls cover the unification move, per-app availability, allow/block status and org-wide defaults, not catalogue export.
claims.fix: Remove the Before rollout bullet beginning 'Export the agent and app catalogue from the Teams admin center as CSV'; this checklist control has no controls-table row.

claims.claim: The supplied descriptions change availability and installation management without describing new actions performed by agents or apps.
claims.quote: Microsoft is rolling out a new feature to streamline how app and agent availability and installation is managed across Teams, Outlook, and Microsoft 365 Copilot.

claims.where: Why it matters: second paragraph; Open questions
claims.claim: The supplied notice does not specify how Phase 3 resolves differences between the admin centres.
claims.quote: Searched: "unified app management" "Phase 3" differences. Read MC796790 and learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/uam-tac-mac; the notice promises additional details later, and Learn documents choices in the administrator-run wizard rather than Phase 3 conflict resolution.
